name: Annular Erythema of Infancy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Annular Erythema of Infancy

criteria.description: Presence of annular, erythematous, and arcuate plaques with central clearing
Onset within the first year of life
Spontaneous resolution of lesions without scarring within weeks to months
Lack of systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise
Histopathological findings showing perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate without vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; biopsy is supportive but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Annular erythematous plaques with central clearing
searchTerms: ring-shaped red plaques with clear center
circular red skin patches clearing in middle

pathognomonic.symptomName: Transient arcuate skin lesions resolving without scarring
searchTerms: arcuate skin spots that heal without scars

common.symptomName: Lesions predominantly on trunk and proximal limbs
searchTerms: rash mainly on trunk and upper arms
lesions mostly on body and proximal limbs
skin spots on torso and limbs

common.symptomName: Absence of systemic symptoms such as fever or malaise
Spontaneous resolution of lesions within weeks to months
searchTerms: lesions that go away on their own

occasional.symptomName: Occasional mild lymphadenopathy near lesion sites
searchTerms: mild swollen lymph nodes near rash

occasional.symptomName: Episodic recurrence of lesions over several months
searchTerms: lesions that come and go over months

rare.symptomName: Mild eosinophilia on peripheral blood count
Histopathological evidence of mild perivascular edema
searchTerms: skin biopsy showing mild blood vessel swelling

rare.symptomName: Rare association with mild systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: rare mild fever with skin symptoms

laboratory: Normal or mild eosinophilia in peripheral blood
other: Histopathology: perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate without vasculitis

distinguishingFeatures: Erythema annulare centrifugum typically affects older children and adults
Lesions have trailing scale inside the advancing edge
Often associated with underlying infections or malignancies
Urticarial lesions are transient, lasting less than 24 hours
Lesions are pruritic wheals rather than annular plaques
Often associated with systemic allergic symptoms
Fungal infection confirmed by KOH preparation
Lesions have scaling and active borders

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as persistent fever
Lesions failing to resolve or worsening over time
Signs of vasculitis or ulceration in skin lesions
